title: Golden Hour Ruin pass: bright aspect-aware renderer, mobile framing, card copy
summary: 'Golden Hour Ruin' redesign (opaque golden sky, warm exposure). Key rendering lesson: MeshStandardMaterial with vertexColors:true but no geometry color attribute multiplies instance colors to near-black — the real 'darkness' cause. Also aspect-aware mobile framing; suite-flake lessons (scroll-behavior:smooth staled rect reads → force instant scroll; boundary-exact aims graze raycaster boxes → aim at cell centers). Retired-lab lineage (n15).

title: Redesign Explosion page as Golden Hour Ruin: bright renderer, mobile framing, card copy
Fix per-part destruction: ghost voxels removed by world_version render sync, condemned members stop bearing load
summary: Attempted fix for per-part destruction (broken parts floated or stayed intact): rebuild the InstancedMesh whenever core worldVersion moves, and stop doomed voxels seeding/routing support so the whole transitive doom set gets timers in one fixpoint solve. Verified headless, but the bug persisted in practice — leading to the demolition lab's retirement at n15.

title: fix(explosion): render doom-cascade breaks and condemn hangers at solver fixpoint
Explosion fresh start: Ember Lantern replaces the demolition lab; dark page shell restored
summary: Decision: demolition lab retired (per-part bug survived two fix rounds); replaced by the LOCKED 'Ember Lantern' — 600 shards on one InstancedMesh, re-posed between rest/flight and never created/destroyed, so a mid-air ghost is unrepresentable (no solver, version counter, or second mesh). TypeScript-only; wasm core dropped from the render path (files kept). Owner-liked dark shell restored. Lesson: a center PointLight can't light a convex shard's outward faces → shards use MeshBasicMaterial.

title: Rebuild Explosion as Ember Lantern: single-state shard sim, dark page shell restored
Explosion goes GPGPU: shard physics moved into fragment shaders, CPU path kept as fallback
summary: Ember Lantern goes GPGPU: 600-shard state in ping-pong RGBA32F textures, fragment shaders integrate the physics and the vertex shader texelFetches state; detonate.ts branches gpu/cpu on EXT_color_buffer_float with the CPU InstancedMesh kept as fallback. Landing card names the GPU physics. Lesson: step shards only while detonating/settling — unconditional stepping collapsed the pristine lantern before any click.

title: Explosion goes GPGPU: shard physics in fragment shaders, minimal page copy
Owner verdict on the GPGPU Ember Lantern: 'i like this'
summary: First explicit owner approval of the Explosion piece after the GPGPU pass (ece801d). The verdict validates the kept direction: fragment-shader physics on ping-pong float textures with the CPU path as fallback, minimal one-line copy on the landing card and project page. Future passes should evolve this concept, not redesign it; remaining polish (if any) should stay within the locked single-source-of-truth law.
